references.text: Direct narrative continuation of the same event (Isaac's meal before the blessing) from Esau's perspective.
Direct narrative cause and effect; the verse expresses the requirement that must be fulfilled before the meal in the source verse can take place.
Thematic contrast: Eliezer's patience (he does not eat until he has spoken his piece) versus Isaac's impulsiveness (eats in order to bless).
Typological parallel: Isaac's meal as a bearer of blessing presupposes the Lord's Supper, where bread becomes the means of God's presence.
